Raksaksri2023_10-18178-ijesd-2023-14-3-2.reason: Field experiment in identical 2.84 m2 ponds with an uncovered control pond. Free-floating LAF-filled PET bottles at 25/50/75/100% cover. The mean ESE for each cover level is reported numerically in the text, and weekly evaporation rates are plotted.
Raksaksri2023_10-18178-ijesd-2023-14-3-2.same_study_as: Benjaoran, Raksaksri & Settakhumpoo 2023, Experimentation of Evaporation Reduction by a Use of Plastic Bottles Covering, Water Conservation & Management 7(2):114-121, doi 10.26480/wcm.02.2023.114.121 (same ponds and same 12 weeks of data; that report adds raft, empty-bottle and assorted-plastic ponds)
Raksaksri2023_10-18178-ijesd-2023-14-3-2.notes: Design: five white PE ponds, 1.90 m diameter, water surface 2.84 m2, filled to 0.50 m (about 1.40 m3) and refilled when below 0.20 m. Site: Nakhon Ratchasima (14.90N 102.01E). Pond 1 is the uncovered control; a Class A pan sits beside the ponds. Cover = free-floating 600 ml PET bottles (0.240 x 0.065 m) filled with laminated aluminium-foil bags. Densest-packing coverage of bottles = 91.2% (p. 214). Water level read daily with a vernier and averaged weekly over 12 weeks. S values are the mean ESE reported on p. 217. E values are the 12-week means of the weekly points in Fig. 5 (p. 216), extracted exactly from the PDF vector graphics. S computed from those E means is 0.191/0.305/0.577/0.616, and the mean of the 12 weekly ratios is 0.191/0.305/0.579/0.618; both are about 2-3 points below the reported ESE, so the difference is not explained by averaging weekly ratios (perhaps daily ratios or a different data window). The plotted data are identical to Fig. 6 of Benjaoran et al. 2023. Meteorological variables were measured but not reported. Initial results; the experiment is described as ongoing.

Benjaoran2023_10-26480-wcm-02-2023-114-1.reason: Same 8-pond PET-bottle experiment at Suranaree University as Raksaksri et al. 2023. The coverage series (ponds 1-5) uses the same 12 weeks of data: Fig. 6 here is identical to Raksaksri Fig. 5, which was confirmed by extracting the plotted vector coordinates from both PDFs. This report adds three conditions that appear only here: raft pattern (pond 6), empty bottles (pond 7) and assorted-plastic-filled bottles (pond 8), all at 50% cover. Rows are extracted for all seven covered ponds.
Benjaoran2023_10-26480-wcm-02-2023-114-1.same_study_as: Raksaksri, Benjaoran & Settakhumpoo 2023, Experimentation of Evaporation Suppression by Various Plastic Bottles Coverage Area, Int. J. Environ. Sci. Dev. 14(3):212-218 (doi printed as 10.18178/ijesd.2023.14.3.1436)
Benjaoran2023_10-26480-wcm-02-2023-114-1.notes: Design: eight identical white PE ponds, 1.90 m diameter and 0.60 m high, water surface 2.84 m2, depth 0.50 m and refilled when below 0.20 m. Site: Nakhon Ratchasima, 14.90N 102.01E, 183 m a.s.l. Pond 1 is an uncovered control; a Class A pan and a rain gauge stood beside the ponds. Treatments (Table 2, p. 117): P2 LAF-filled 25% free; P3 LAF 50% free; P4 LAF 75% free; P5 LAF 100% free; P6 LAF 50% raft; P7 empty 50% free; P8 assorted-plastic-filled 50% free. Bottles are 600 ml PET, 0.240 m long x 0.065 m wide, each covering 1.43e-2 m2 (assumed half-submerged). Densest packing of bottles = 91.2%. Evaporation was read daily and averaged weekly over 12 weeks. No numerical results are given; all E values are the plotted weekly points, extracted exactly from the PDF vector graphics (Excel line charts; axis calibrated on the 1.0 and 6.0 tick labels) and averaged over the 12 weeks. S = 1 - mean(Ec)/mean(Eo). For ponds 2-5, prefer the ESE values Raksaksri 2023 reports in its text (21.8/32.7/59.2/63.3%); the figure-derived values here are about 2 points lower. The ESE equation is misprinted as (1-Ei)/Ec x 100. Meteorological data were measured but not reported. The paper calls the experiment ongoing (initial results).
